en: start of regular ship or flight service

examples.ko: 새 항공사의 제주 노선 취항이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: The new airline's launch of a Jeju route has been decided.

examples.ko: 이 배는 다음 달 첫 취항을 앞두고 있어요.
examples.en: This ship is about to make its first voyage next month.
They are holding a sale to mark the new route.

examples.ko: 취항 소식에 공항 주변이 들떠 있어요.
examples.en: The area around the airport is excited by the news of the new service.

examples.ko: 직항 노선의 취항이 늘어서 여행하기 편해졌어요.
examples.en: More direct routes have launched, so traveling has become easier.
On the first day of service, they even handed out souvenirs.

explain: 항공기나 여객선이 어떤 노선에 처음 다니기 시작하는 것을 말해서 뉴스에서 '신규 취항'으로 자주 써요. 계속 다니는 것을 말하는 '운항'과는 달라요. 비행기뿐 아니라 배에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 항공사는 다음 달 신규 취항을 발표했어요.
phrases.en: The airline announced a new route launch for next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 노선이 처음 생길 때 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in the news when a brand-new route is started.

phrases.en: Travel has become easier because there are more routes in service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항공사나 선박 회사가 다니는 노선을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the routes an airline or shipping company serves.

phrases.en: A ceremony for the new passenger ship's maiden service was held at Busan port.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 배나 비행기가 처음 다니기 시작할 때 하는 기념 행사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony held when a new ship or plane begins service.

explain_en: It refers to a plane or ship starting service on a route, and appears in news as '신규 취항' (new service launch). It differs from '운항', which is about operating regularly. It can be used for ships as well as planes.

examples.en: Oil-producing countries agreed to cut oil production.
The factory decided to cut production when demand fell.
Prices rose on news of reduced crop production.

examples.ko: 감산이 길어지면 일자리가 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If production cuts last long, jobs could be lost.

examples.ko: 반도체 업체들이 감산으로 가격 하락을 막으려 해요.
examples.en: Semiconductor makers are trying to stop price drops by cutting production.

examples.ko: 이번 감산은 수요가 줄어서 어쩔 수 없었대요.
examples.en: I heard this production cut was unavoidable because demand dropped.

explain: 생산량을 줄이는 일을 가리키는 경제 뉴스 단어고, 반대말은 '증산'이에요. 보통 '감산에 들어가다', '감산을 결정하다'처럼 쓰고 일상 대화에서는 '생산을 줄이다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The car company has started cutting production.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생산량 줄이기를 시작할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when production cuts begin.

phrases.en: The factory will cut production from next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '감산'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 감산 plus '하다' as a verb.

phrases.en: Demand dropped, so we reduce production.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '감산' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday phrase used instead of 감산.

explain_en: Cutting factory or industrial output; used in economy and business news. It is an economic news word for reducing output, and its opposite is '증산'. It is used in phrases like '감산에 들어가다' and '감산을 결정하다', while in daily talk people say '생산을 줄이다'.

en: to decrease; to be reduced in amount or number

examples.en: Customers decrease in winter.
Accidents decreased a lot compared to last year.
If trash decreases, it is good for the environment.
The rate of decrease is fast.
The cost that doesn't go down is the problem.
The population will keep decreasing.

explain: '감소하다'와 뜻이 같고, 보통은 '감소하다'를 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '증가'예요. 사람 수, 비용, 사고처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것이 줄 때 써요.

phrases.en: Customers decrease in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감소되다'보다 더 많이 쓰는 기본형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more commonly used form compared with 감소되다.

phrases.en: The number of customers has dropped a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler and more natural word for everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The number of children keeps decreasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 줄고 있는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change that is still going on.

explain_en: Goes down by itself — numbers, amounts; passive, formal. It means the same as '감소하다', and '감소하다' is the more common form. The opposite is '증가'. Use it when things you can measure in numbers, like people, costs, or accidents, go down.

dis.h: numbers or amounts simply go down

p.n: 축소되다 is for scale or size, not a count of guests.

en: to reduce an amount; to cut

examples.en: The company decided to reduce this year's bonus.
When I explained my situation, they reduced my fine.
I checked whether there is a system that reduces hospital bills.

examples.ko: 소득이 줄어서 보험료를 감액할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can get your premium reduced because your income dropped.
If the subsidy is reduced, household budgets get tight.
The deal was canceled even though the deposit was reduced.

explain: '줄이다'나 구어체 '깎다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 서류, 계약, 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 반대말은 '증액하다'예요.

phrases.en: Because things were hard for me, they reduced my rent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 사정을 봐서 돈을 줄여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reducing an amount out of consideration for someone.

phrases.en: My allowance was reduced because of lateness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 줄어든 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form from the side whose money was reduced.

phrases.en: Please take a bit off the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 표현이고 '감액하다'보다 가벼워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple spoken word, lighter than 감액하다.

explain_en: Lowering a price, fee, or payment figure itself. It is more formal than '줄이다' or the casual '깎다', so you see it in paperwork, contracts and the news. Its opposite is '증액하다'.

examples.ko: 새 앱의 개발비가 생각보다 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The new app's development cost was more than I expected.
To cut development costs, we didn't hire more staff.
I heard new drug development costs hundreds of billions of won.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 개발비만 오십억 원이 넘었어요.
examples.en: The development cost of this game alone exceeded five billion won.
The government supports technology development costs.

examples.ko: 개발비 때문에 가격을 올릴 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the development cost, we have no choice but to raise the price.

explain: 제품이나 기술을 새로 만드는 데 드는 돈이에요. '생활비', '교육비'처럼 '~비'가 붙은 말이에요. 'N 개발비'처럼 앞에 개발 대상을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 게임을 만드는 데 개발비가 많이 들었어요.
phrases.en: Making the game cost a lot in development expenses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 드는 것은 '들다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Costs are expressed with 들다.

phrases.en: I made it myself to save on development costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 덜 쓰려고 할 때 '아끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 아끼다 is used when trying to spend less money.

phrases.en: How much does app development cost?
phrases.nuance_ko: 개발 대상을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the thing being developed before the word.

explain_en: It is the money spent on creating a new product or technology. It is built like '생활비' and '교육비', with '비' attached. You put the thing developed in front, like 'N 개발비'.

en: to be traded; to be dealt

examples.ko: 이 책은 중고 시장에서 비싸게 거래돼요.
examples.en: This book sells for a high price on the used market.
That painting sold for 100 million won.
The stock is being actively traded.
Don't buy items that are traded illegally.
I wonder how much the house will go for.

examples.ko: 거래된 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the transaction history in the app.

explain: 물건이나 주식이 사고팔리는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 주어이면 '거래하다'를 써요. '중고 거래', '직거래'처럼 명사 '거래'로 훨씬 자주 쓰고, '억 원에 거래되다'처럼 '에'로 가격을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 이 물건은 인터넷에서 많이 거래되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This item is traded a lot online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 사고팔리는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that is currently and continually being bought and sold.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 중고로 거래돼도 값이 높아요.
phrases.en: This bag is still pricey even when traded secondhand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 물건이 아니라 쓰던 물건이 팔릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a used item, not a new one, is being sold.

phrases.example: 그 물건은 시장에서 거의 거래되지 않아요.
phrases.en: That item is hardly traded in the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고파는 일이 거의 없을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when there is almost no buying or selling.

explain_en: Passive; goods or stocks are traded at some price (싸게 거래되다). It describes goods or stocks being bought and sold. If a person is the subject, use 거래하다 instead. The noun 거래 is much more common, as in 중고 거래 and 직거래, and you add the price with 에, like 억 원에 거래되다.

examples.en: Today's stock trading volume was higher than usual.
Stocks with low trading volume are hard to buy and sell.

examples.ko: 연휴 때문에 중고 시장의 거래량이 크게 줄었어요.
examples.en: The holiday sharply cut the volume of trades in the secondhand market.

examples.ko: 이 앱의 하루 거래량은 수만 건이에요.
examples.en: This app handles tens of thousands of transactions a day.
As home prices rose, the volume of apartment sales changed too.

examples.ko: 거래량을 보면 요즘 인기 있는 상품을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Looking at the trading volume, you can tell which products are popular lately.

explain: 주식, 부동산, 상품을 사고판 양이나 횟수를 말해요. 오고 간 돈의 크기를 말할 때는 '거래액'을 써서 구별해요. '거래량이 늘다', '거래량이 급증하다'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Trading volume rose before the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고판 양이 많아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount traded has increased.

phrases.en: Trading volume surged after the new product came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 늘었을 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for a sudden sharp rise.

phrases.en: Trading volume dropped, so prices fell too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고파는 사람이 적어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fewer people are buying and selling.

explain_en: Quantity traded, in units or number of deals (주식 거래량) It means the amount or number of trades in stocks, real estate or goods. For the size of the money that changed hands, '거래액' is used instead. It is common in news as '거래량이 늘다' or '거래량이 급증하다'.

en: to plunge; to plummet; to decrease sharply

examples.ko: 비가 계속 오면 가게 손님이 격감해요.
examples.en: If it keeps raining, customers at the shop drop sharply.
This year's sales plunged compared with last year.

examples.ko: 인구가 격감하면 학교도 문을 닫아야 해요.
examples.en: If the population plummets, schools also have to close.
My income dropped sharply, so I'm worried about living costs.
The number of visitors is expected to fall sharply.
Let's find out why the number of tourists suddenly plummeted.

explain: '수가 격감하다'처럼 줄어드는 것을 주어로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 줄다', '많이 줄다'라고 하고, '격감하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '급증하다'예요.

phrases.en: In winter the number of customers drops sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격감하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 글 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 격감하다, in written style.

phrases.en: The number of customers has dropped a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in casual conversation.

phrases.en: The number of births is plunging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 줄어드는 중일 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 있다' to say the drop is happening now.

explain_en: Amounts or counts, like customers or sales, decrease suddenly. The thing that decreases is the subject, as in '수가 격감하다'. In daily talk people say '확 줄다' or '많이 줄다', while '격감하다' appears more in news and writing. The opposite is '급증하다'.

t90.ax: This year's sales plunged compared with last year.

en: to settle accounts; to close the books

examples.ko: 연말에는 가계부를 보면서 한 해를 결산해요.
examples.en: At the end of the year, I look over my budget book and sum up the year.

examples.ko: 경리 직원이 월말에 장부를 결산하는 중이에요.
examples.en: The accountant is closing the books for the month.

examples.ko: 올해 활동을 결산해 보니 아쉬운 점이 많아요.
examples.en: Looking back at this year's activities, there's a lot I regret.
The broadcaster wrapped up the year's best songs.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 한 학기를 결산하고 싶어요.
examples.en: After exams, I want to look back on the semester.

examples.ko: 내년에 결산할 때 웃을 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope I can smile when I look back next year.

explain: 회사나 가게가 돈 계산을 마무리할 때 써요. 연말에 '한 해를 결산하다'처럼 한 해 일을 돌아볼 때도 많이 써요. '정산하다'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 정산은 받을 돈과 줄 돈을 맞추는 일에 더 가까워요.

phrases.example: 연말 결산 방송에서 올해 인기 노래를 소개했어요.
phrases.en: The year-end review show introduced this year's popular songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 일을 돌아보며 정리하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for looking back over and summing up the year.

phrases.en: The accounting team is preparing the financial report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 돈 계산이 끝난 뒤 내놓는 보고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the report given at work once the accounts are closed.

phrases.en: After the trip, my friends and I settled up the costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받을 돈과 줄 돈을 맞출 때는 '결산하다' 대신 '정산하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For matching what is owed and what is due, use 정산하다 instead of 결산하다.

explain_en: It is used when a company or shop wraps up its accounts. It is also very common at year-end, as in '한 해를 결산하다', to look back on the year. It is easy to mix up with 정산하다, which is closer to settling who owes what.

examples.en: A big donor gave a scholarship fund to the school.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 고액 연봉으로 사람을 뽑아요.
examples.en: That company hires people with a very high salary.

examples.ko: 현금으로 고액을 내는 사람은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people pay a large sum in cash.
More students are getting expensive private tutoring.
The hospital bill is a large sum, so I am worried.
It is a contest with a big prize.

explain: 고액은 '고액 연봉', '고액 기부'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요. 반대말은 '소액'이고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '큰돈'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Expensive private tutoring is a burden for parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 많이 드는 서비스 앞에 '고액'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '고액' before a service that costs a lot of money.

phrases.en: It is dangerous to carry a large amount of cash.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고액의'를 쓰면 돈의 양이 큰 것을 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '고액의' clearly says the amount of money is large.

phrases.example: 그 일은 고액 연봉을 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can get a high salary in that job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이 아주 많은 일자리를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for jobs with a very high salary.

explain_en: Sino-Korean; high amount per unit or transaction (고액 연봉, 고액 기부) 고액 is often placed before another noun, as in 고액 연봉 or 고액 기부. Its opposite is 소액, and in everyday talk people also just say 큰돈.

en: to fall headlong; to fall head-first

examples.en: I slipped on the stairs and almost tumbled headlong down.
Right after the announcement, the company's stock price plunged.
Watching the stock price plummet makes me anxious.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀 성적이 곤두박질하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team's results have been going downhill fast lately.
The bird sees its food and dives headfirst into the water.

examples.ko: 기온이 하루 만에 영하로 곤두박질해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the temperature plunged below zero in just one day.

explain: '곤두박질치다'라고도 많이 말해요. 몸이 거꾸로 떨어질 때뿐 아니라 주가, 성적, 인기가 갑자기 크게 떨어질 때도 써요. 반대로 값이 확 오를 때는 '치솟다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The temperature suddenly plunged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning, and used more often.

phrases.en: I want to revive my plunging popularity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun.

phrases.en: I'm scared my grades will plunge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길까 걱정할 때 '-ㄹ까 봐'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ까 봐', it expresses worry that something bad may happen.

explain_en: Less common variant of (곤두박질치다) with the same literal meaning. People also say '곤두박질치다'. It is used for a body falling head-first, and also when stock prices, grades or popularity suddenly drop a lot. The opposite, when prices shoot up, is '치솟다'.

t90.ax: Watching the stock price plummet makes me anxious.

examples.en: This channel earns its income from advertising fees.

examples.ko: 광고료가 비싸서 작은 가게는 부담이 커요.
examples.en: Ad fees are expensive, so it's a big burden for small shops.
The advertising fee differs depending on the broadcast time slot.

examples.ko: 광고료를 내면 검색 결과 맨 위에 나와요.
examples.en: If you pay an ad fee, you appear at the top of the search results.

examples.ko: 유명한 모델을 쓰면 광고료가 훨씬 올라가요.
examples.en: If you use a famous model, the ad costs go up a lot.
Please tell me the price including the advertising fee.

explain: 신문이나 방송, 사이트가 광고를 실어 주고 받는 돈이라는 느낌이 강해요. 광고를 내는 쪽 입장에서는 '광고비'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Broadcasters receive advertising fees and air the ads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 실어 주는 쪽에서 돈을 받는 입장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side that carries ads and receives the money.

phrases.en: The shop owner paid an advertising fee to the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 내는 쪽에서 돈을 내는 입장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side that places the ad and pays.

phrases.en: I spent a lot on advertising this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 내는 쪽에서 쓰는 돈을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for money spent by the party running the ad.

explain_en: It carries the sense of money that a newspaper, broadcaster or site charges for running an ad. From the advertiser's side, people also commonly say '광고비'.

examples.ko: 학술지 구독료가 비싸서 학교 도서관을 통해 읽어요.
examples.en: The journal subscription fee is expensive, so I read it through the school library.
The newspaper subscription fee went up again.

examples.ko: 월 구독료를 내면 영화를 무제한으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay a monthly subscription fee, you can watch unlimited movies.
I set the subscription fee to be paid automatically by card.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 구독료 없이 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this app without a subscription fee.
The subscription fee was a burden, so I cancelled the service.

explain: 신문, 잡지뿐 아니라 요즘은 음악, 영상, 앱 서비스에 내는 정기 요금도 구독료라고 해요. '월 구독료', '구독료를 내다'처럼 써요. 서비스를 그만두는 건 '구독을 해지하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I pay the subscription fee for a video service every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정기적으로 돈을 낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means paying money on a regular basis.

phrases.en: The monthly subscription fee is 10,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 달마다 내는 요금을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the fee paid each month.

phrases.en: The subscription fee was a burden, so I cancelled my subscription.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서비스 이용을 그만둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you stop using the service.

explain_en: Besides newspapers and magazines, it now also covers regular fees for music, video and app services. You say '월 구독료' and '구독료를 내다'. Quitting a service is '구독을 해지하다'.

examples.en: When prices rise, consumers' purchasing power falls.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 구매력 높은 중산층이 많아요.
examples.en: This country has many middle-class people with high purchasing power.

examples.ko: 월급이 같아도 환율에 따라 구매력은 달라져요.
examples.en: Even with the same salary, purchasing power changes with the exchange rate.

examples.ko: 정부는 청년의 구매력을 높일 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is looking for ways to raise young people's purchasing power.

examples.ko: 구매력에 맞는 가격으로 물건을 팔아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to sell goods at prices that match what customers can afford.

examples.ko: 구매력까지 고려하면 이 도시가 더 비싸요.
examples.en: If you take purchasing power into account too, this city is more expensive.

explain: 가진 돈으로 물건을 살 수 있는 힘이에요. 월급이 같아도 물가가 오르면 구매력은 떨어져요. 단순한 소득이나 재산과는 달라요. '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다', '구매력을 높이다'처럼 경제 뉴스에서 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 월급을 올리면 사람들의 구매력을 높일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Raising wages can increase people's purchasing power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 더 많이 살 수 있게 한다는 뜻으로, 경제 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means helping people afford more, used in talk about the economy.

phrases.en: If income is low, purchasing power is low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살 수 있는 힘이 약하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the ability to buy things is weak.

phrases.example: 회사는 구매력이 있는 소비자를 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: The company is looking for consumers with purchasing power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 살 돈이 충분한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who have enough money to buy things.

explain_en: It means how much you can buy with the money you have. Even with the same salary, purchasing power drops when prices rise, so it differs from income or wealth itself. It is common in economic news, as in '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다' and '구매력을 높이다'.
